title: Trumpet
reference_instrument: University of Iowa MIS Bb trumpet (Bach 180S37 Stradivarius, 1987, per MISBbtrumpet.html)
summary: Limits: two routes that cannot be combined (G3, Bb3, E4 on a linear bore with a flanged modal bell; F4, Bb4, D5 on a nonlinear gas bore with a piston bell, except that D5's bore ends in the plane-mode equivalent of a flanged multimodal mouth and only its listener is the baffled piston); valves only as derived loops for E4 and G3; no A5; too dark on the modal-bell pages (hold centroid 773 to 992 Hz, recordings 1371 to 1399 Hz). A Bb trumpet played by a lip valve: the note is the lock the loop finds, and no pitch is an input. Bore: the 34-station profile of Tournemenne and Chabassier (2019), with its main tube (11.66 mm) and bell (122.24 mm) set to the manufacturer's printed numbers for the Bach 180S37 on Bb3, E4, F4 and D5 (G3 and Bb4 play earlier renders that predate the change, with the profile's rounded 11.64 and 11.65 mm and 122.0 mm). Lip: Cullen's (2000) embouchure 19, a trombone-rig artificial lip, not a trumpeter's. Mouth pressure: a sustain of 3.5 x 7 Pa/Hz x the note (Fletcher and Tarnopolsky 1999), reached by a 1.3-times leap held 0.1 s on G3, Bb3 and E4 (shape read from one print, Hruška, Švejda and Guštar 2015) and by a 14 kPa ramp on F4, Bb4 and D5; each pre-stress is a player's setting chosen from a first render's pitch. On D5 the blowing pressure feeds the lip through a finite mouth (a 22.24 cm3 store and a 0.14 cm2 nozzle, both borrowed from other players' anatomy). On D5 the bell wall is also a brass shell coupled to the bore (a uniform 0.4826 mm shell of cartridge brass with its throat ring clamped, its three axisymmetric modes, 1031 to 6859 Hz, driven by the bore cell by cell; thickness and loss factor both borrowed): against the same card without it, rendered by the same binary, it moves the held note by -0.11 cents and the level by -0.08 dB, no audible change is claimed, no shell mode lies in the 500 to 800 Hz band of the bell resonances measured by Gorman et al. (2014), and the grader's count ties at 11 of 15 (10 strict) with the distance 15.095 to 14.899; the page's clip is the 32 kHz render of 2026-11-11 (md5 3f0b674689f2). Flow noise at the lips (Oldham and Ukpoho 1990, extrapolated) is on every page. On G3, Bb3, E4 and D5 the lip's flow area rises as the gap to the power 1.4, an exponent borrowed from a trombonist's measured lip opening area (Copley and Strong 1996) through an authored power law, because renders of Bb3 and E4 with the measured per-note value fell on the count, and G3's with the measured 1.650 (Bromage, Campbell and Gilbert 2010, together with a 48 kHz rate) read 6 of 14 against the 7 of its earlier 32 kHz page, which replaced it on 2026-11-10; no trumpet lip-opening area is printed, and Bb4 and F4 do not carry the row because a render of each did not post (F4's with the measured 1.900 does not sound its note). The three modal-bell pages hold one uniform full-breath gas in the bore, which moves the held note by +1.40 cents on G3, +4.80 on Bb3 and +7.21 on E4 (the bore's own impedance peaks move 10.8), and their listener carries the exterior gas's classical absorption, which changes no band by more than 0.033 dB. A stand-in bore, not the recorded Bach 180S37's. Since 2026-11-10 Bb4 plays an earlier render under the best-count rule, the one this page showed until 2026-11-03 (git 88656aac2): the plain trumpet/render.sh card on a linear bore with the baffled-disk receiver at 1.524 m. It carries none of the rows named for Bb4 on this card (no nonlinear gas bore, no printed bore and bell diameters, no flow noise at the lips, no flanged modal bell), so the statements above and below that give Bb4 the gas-bore route, the printed diameters, the flow noise or its place among all six pages describe its later page, which stays in the page's history. Since 2026-11-10 G3 also plays an earlier render under the best-count rule, the one this page showed until 2026-11-08 (set trumpet/G3-observer-gas, rendered 2026-11-07, 32 kHz in the engine, 7 of 14 and 7 strict, graded once as first processed): the flanged modal bell, the three-semitone valve loop, the print-shaped attack, the breath bore gas, the observer gas, flow noise and q 1.4, with the profile's rounded diameters and without the later pages' printed diameters, 48 kHz rate and q 1.650; the statements above and below that give G3 those rows describe its later pages, which stay in the page's history.
physics_present: fs-couple brass_loop: a one-degree-of-freedom outward-striking lip (Cullen 2000, embouchure 19: resonance 237 Hz, quality factor 12, inverse mass 0.072 m2/kg, 9 mm wide, 0.25 mm rest gap; the width and gap are Cullen's own estimates) with a Bernoulli aperture solved implicitly with the mouthpiece junction. Blowing pressure and lip pre-stress are gestures on the shared canonical schedule

The bore: the 34-station profile published with Tournemenne and Chabassier (2019), copied from the openwind example file, 1.4187 m long, valves straightened; on Bb3, E4, F4 and D5 (G3 and Bb4 play earlier renders that predate the change) the main tube (.459 in = 11.66 mm) and the last bell radius (4 13/16 in = 122.24 mm across) are the manufacturer's printed numbers for the Bach Stradivarius 180S37 (Conn-Selmer brochure; a dealer's listing prints the same), in place of the profile's 11.64 and 11.65 mm and 122.0 mm, with the cones either side of the cylinder meeting it at the same 5.83 mm radius and no length changed. Against the pages that carried the rounded numbers the held note moved by +0.29 cents on G3, +0.52 on Bb3, +0.24 on E4, +0.03 on D5, +0.05 on F4 and -0.22 on Bb4, the level by under 0.02 dB, and the grader's count tied on all six (7, 5 and 6 of 14, 11 of 15, 5 of 14 and 7 of 14, no row crossing a ruler); on D5, a nonlinear V2 page, the unchanged card rendered on the same binary had reproduced the previous clip byte for byte, so the four radii are the only change there; the closure build wrote Bb4's previous clip byte for byte from its unchanged card, and F4 has no unchanged-card render on any build (the same binary wrote D5's byte for byte)

G3, Bb3 and E4: a linear multimodal transfer-matrix bore with viscothermal loss, a flanged modal radiation load at the bell (modal_baffle), and the listener by a finite-distance Rayleigh integral over every mouth mode, 1.524 m on axis. The mouth-flow ladder runs at a declared tail tolerance of 2e-6 (mouth_flow_tail_tol on the card)

F4, Bb4 and D5: a nonlinear Euler gas bore with Zwikker-Kosten wall memory (128 poles at a tolerance of 1e-2, 20 to 8000 Hz), a baffled-piston bell at the bore end (on D5 the bore's radiating end is instead the plane-mode equivalent of a complete flanged multimodal mouth, the opt-in mouth_load modal row of 8 modes, 2 extra slices, a 6000 Hz claim band, 10 Hz bins and a tail tolerance of 1e-10, set before any render and not fitted to a recording: a lossless modal solve at the mouth radius the render's provenance records for the load, 60.89 mm (the bore's end radius is 61.12 mm), kept as 2190 taps with a dropped tail energy of 9.96e-11 and evaluated to 21510 Hz; the receiver stays the baffled-piston Rayleigh integral of the plane mouth flow, the flanged modal bell record itself is still not combined with the nonlinear bore, and a plane bore on this load sits up to 5.6 cents sharp of the multimodal bore from about 400 Hz) and dry air from the thermochemical gas packs; on D5 also a finite upstream mouth (the mouth_reservoir row): a 22.24 cm3 store fed through a 0.14 cm2 nozzle from the held blowing pressure, the volume the oropharynx of 66 trumpet players at rest (Cilingir, Ghoneima and Eckert 2023, a lower bound) and the opening the glottis of one trumpet player blowing (Kaburagi et al. 2011), both borrowed, with no neck inertia and no lung; the flow noise is offered to the lip in series at the stored gas's own temperature (an isothermal modulation) and its work is rejected as heat. Against the D5 page on the printed bore the grader's count ties at 11 of 15, the held note moves +0.85 cents, the level -0.64 dB and the band energy above 1 kHz falls by 0.6 to 1.9 dB

Flow noise at the lips on every page (the constriction_noise row): a pressure source in each third octave, sized by the blowing pressure and the cup radius of the card's own first bore record, from the printed law of Oldham and Ukpoho (1990, as reprinted by Guedel 2005). It is an extrapolation from dampers and plates in a large duct at 10 to 25 m/s, and no level was set

The attack on G3, Bb3 and E4: a 50 ms ramp to 1.3 times the card's own sustain, held 0.1 s, then 50 ms down to the sustain. The 1.3 and the 0.1 s are the leap over the plateau and its duration read from the plot of Hruška, Švejda and Guštar (2015, Vienna Talk on Music Acoustics, Figs 4-5: one semi-professional player on a glass mouthpiece, a pilot); their pressure level is not used

The lip aperture on Bb3 (the lip_area_exponent row, q = 1.4): the flow area is width x gap x (gap / rest gap)^(q - 1), so it rises faster than the gap, with the card's own 0.25 mm rest gap. The 1.4 is borrowed, not measured on a trumpet: Copley and Strong (1996, Table AI) print a trombonist's lip opening area against height, peak 34 mm2 and mean 15.4 mm2, which read as q 1.35 and 1.44 on the authored power law; the trombone page's rest gap is 0.53 mm against this card's 0.25 mm. No trumpet lip-opening area is printed, and q also stands in for part of the lip's short swing. On Bb3 the hold centroid rises by 25 % and the hold sits 2.8 cents higher; the grader's count goes from 4 to 5 of 14 (strict 3 = 3), with the spectrogram difference, partial level trajectories, partial frequencies, fundamental frequency, harmonics-to-noise and attack time farther from the recording and the spectral distance, harmonic level pattern, spectral centroid over time and five others closer

The same lip_area_exponent row, q = 1.4, on G3, E4 and D5. On G3 the row alone moves the held note +6.21 cents and, with the breath bore, +6.06; on E4 +2.33 and, with the bore, +9.19. On the nonlinear D5 page, at 128 wall poles, the grader's count goes from 9 to 11 of 15, the hold moves +5.73 cents and the fundamental line rises 14.8 %; the clip is brighter than the recording (spectral distance 8.51 to 17.93 dB, harmonic levels 6.39 to 14.27, band envelope 5.62 to 10.85, scalogram 8.49 to 13.07, short-time spectrum 16.01 to 18.01, attack 1.79 to 2.26 octaves of time, cepstral envelope 7.29 to 7.63)

the same uniform breath state in the bore, cup and lip of G3, Bb3 and E4 (a row bore_gas on each page's modal-bell card): it moves the held note by +1.40 cents (G3, the gas alone), +4.80 (Bb3) and +7.21 (E4, the gas alone), that is 13, 44 and 67 % of the bore's own +10.8 cents

on G3, Bb3 and E4, the exterior gas's classical Stokes-Kirchhoff absorption and dispersion along every signed mouth-mode path from the bell to the microphone (a row observer_gas, commit 6ea217153): ties at 7, 5 and 6 of 14, the held note unchanged and no band changed by more than 0.033 dB over 1.524 m of dry 20 C air; no humid-air relaxation law is declared

Two valve notes: E4 adds the second valve's loop (84.36 mm) and G3 a three-semitone loop (268.4 mm), each the bore's 1.4187 m times the equal-tempered length ratio, inserted as straight tube. The lengths are derived, not measured
The fanfare and the slur are one render each on the modal-bell route with the flow-noise row on, so every note change happens inside the simulation

the lip's flow-area exponent as a trombonist's lips measured it, per note (Bromage, Campbell and Gilbert 2010, preprint HAL hal-00474644v1, Table 2; one trombonist, AJ, mezzo forte, high-speed video; 1.2 at Bb1, 1.3 at Bb2, 1.6 at F3, 1.9 at F4; linear interpolation in MIDI between printed notes, no extrapolation; a trombonist's lips on a trombone mouthpiece and not a trumpeter's, a larger borrowing than the tuba's), tried on four pages against their unchanged cards (the four byte controls equal the live clips, so only the exponent changed): G3 with q = 1.650 in place of the 1.4 borrowed from a trombone that the entries above name for G3 (the count tied at 6 of 14; since 2026-11-10 G3 plays its earlier 32 kHz page with q 1.4, 7 of 14, because the 1.650 row and the 48 kHz rate together cost a count: on one binary the 1.650 row alone left 6 of 14, the rate alone left 6 of 14, and with both off the clip was the earlier page's byte for byte and read 7 of 14; the held note +2.15 cents, the level +0.86 dB); Bb3 (q 1.725; 5 to 3 of 14: attack and spectral flux left their rulers) and E4 (q 1.875; 6 to 4 of 14: spectral distance and harmonics-to-noise ratio left theirs) fell and keep 1.4; F4 with q 1.900 ADDED (it carried none) does not sound its note: the strongest line of the clip is 457.3 Hz, a harmonic series on 457.3 Hz (914.6, 1371.7, 1829.0 and 2286.3 Hz at 2 to 5 times) against F4's 349.2 Hz, with a weak line at 360.6 Hz 20.3 dB under it, 404 clipped samples, the held note's level 4.95 dB under the live clip's, a lip that never closes (closed share 0.000 against 0.791; gap maximum 0.570 mm against 1.137 mm) and the grader's refusal (IRPDECOMP_NOT_THE_NAMED_NOTE), so F4 carries no row; Bb4 and D5 lie above the table's top note and are unchanged. On G3, Bb3 and E4 the lip's own motion at the held note changed little (under 2.2 cents, 1.4 dB and 5 percent of lip gap), but the onset grows later, by 0.25 to 0.5 s on G3, about 0.25 s on Bb3 and about 0.5 s on E4: on E4 the clip is non-periodic until about 1.0 s (windowed autocorrelation periodicity 0.202, 0.023 and 0.518 at 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75 s, against 0.960, 0.986 and 0.985 on the live clip; the first lip closure at about 1.0 s against 0.5 to 0.6 s; the bore pressure grows first, 1918 Pa against 693 Pa at 0.4 s) and then locks to a cycle as periodic as the live one (0.985; lip gap maximum 1.633 mm in every 0.1 s window from 1.2 s on; bore pressure 8719 +- 5 Pa). The grader's harmonics-to-noise ratio of the E4 clip fell from 34.919 to 9.258 dB (the recording's is 36.483) because its sustain window (0.15 s to at most 1.10 s of a cut that starts 10 ms before the detected onset, about 0.58 to 1.53 s of the clip) contains that stretch: an approximation of the grader's measure (the energy within 14 Hz of every harmonic against the energy between them, 80 Hz to 10 kHz, without the grader's pitch-holding step) gives 9.1 and 34.8 dB on that window, within 0.2 dB of the grader's two values, and 32.3 to 32.5 dB from 1.0 s on against the live clip's 34.8 to 35.1; the approximation matches the grader on that window only

D5's bell wall (the opt-in bore_wall shell-brass row, landed 2026-11-11 in fs-duct and fs-couple): the flaring end of the bore, from the radius 5.985 mm to the 61.12 mm mouth (229 bore cells), is a MITC3+ shell of revolution of cartridge brass (UNS C26000, MIL-HDBK-698A Table XV: 8525.4 kg/m3, 110.316 GPa, Poisson ratio 0.333) on a 32-sided mesh with its throat ring clamped and the rest free. Its axisymmetric modes below 7000 Hz (the receiver's 6.9 kHz band edge) are driven by the pressures of the bore cells and sweep volume back into the gas, each with a loss factor of 1e-4 (a quality factor of 1e4), and the account of gas work, stored energy, dissipated work and work against the room pressure closes to 4e-15 of its largest term on a test bell. Of the 101 shell modes below 7000 Hz three are axisymmetric: 1031.4 Hz, one between, and 6859.0 Hz. Both numbers of the wall are borrowed and none is a measurement of this bell: the thickness 0.4826 mm (0.019 in, the Bb trumpet bell thickness of Vincent Bach's New York 1951 notebooks as bachloyalist.com prints it; the page does not say whether a notebook figure is the sheet or the finished bell, the recorded instrument is a 1987 Elkhart Bach 180S37, and the same page's own note, which is not a Bach or Conn-Selmer quote, gives 0.025 in for modern Elkhart 180-series bells and 0.020 in for lightweight ones; no render at another thickness was made) and the loss factor (NPTEL course 112104040, Table 9.1, brass, order of loss factor 1e-4: the order of a material and not of a bell; seams, the rim wire and the support only add loss, so the value may lie a decade either side; the count is not scored on it). Against the same card without the two rows rendered by the same binary (a release build of origin 86f4974f5a; 5 h 4 min against 6 h 21 min on ts2 at nice 19), the wall lowers the held note by 0.108 cents (591.2833 to 591.2465 Hz) and the level by 0.077 dB, moves harmonics 2 to 8 by -0.11 to -0.25 dB (the first by +0.07 dB) and the band energy at 0 to 1, 1 to 3 and 3 to 6.9 kHz by +0.07, -0.14 and -0.23 dB; no audible change is claimed. The two waveforms drift apart in phase as the shift accumulates (zero-lag correlation 0.9945 in the first half second and 0.078 in the last), which is not a change of loudness or timbre. The same wall on the D5-res card (md5 36aa4951, the card of the D5 page before the live one, without the modal mouth row) moved the note by 0.104 cents and the level by 0.077 dB, so its effect does not depend on that row at this size. On the grader's kit the control and the wall each read 11 of 15 loose and 10 strict, the page's best-ever count, no measure crosses a ruler in either direction, and the total distance goes from 15.095 to 14.899 (the page live before reads 15.093 from a clip of another binary: the two were not compared byte for byte). Three of the grader's gaps grew, none near its ruler: the trajectory of the partials 2.409 to 2.458 dB, the odd-to-even ratio 0.416 to 0.437 dB and the attack 2.239 to 2.252 octaves of time.
physics_missing: Valves: only E4's second-valve loop and G3's three-semitone loop exist, as straight tube of derived length with none of a real valve's bends or port steps. Every other valve and combination, the tuning slide and valve switching during a note are absent, and the cards hold no measured loop length for this trumpet; no slide length of a Bb trumpet was found in anything opened on 2026-11-09

A5: no hold on the second-valve bore lands on it. At 21.56 kPa, pre-stress 2.56, 2.62 and 2.68 sound the sixth partial, E5; a slur up from pre-stress 2.0 to 2.62 starts on the fifth partial, jumps to E5 and stays there, never reaching A5. A slow sweep of the lip reached A5 only by climbing through every partial, so the lock depends on the path. The A5 page stays recording-only

The two routes cannot be joined: the flanged modal bell needs a linear bore, so the modal-bell pages (G3, Bb3, E4) have no gas nonlinearity, no wave steepening and no wall-material memory, and the gas-bore pages (F4, Bb4, D5) radiate through a piston bell, except that D5's bore ends in the plane-mode equivalent of the flanged multimodal mouth (its listener is still the baffled piston, and the flanged modal bell record itself is still not combined with the nonlinear bore). Each page says which it lacks. A gas-bore render of G3, Bb3 and E4, each with its page's hold and valve loop, was made and not posted: each fell on the count against its modal-bell page (E4 2 of 14 against 5, Bb3 2 against 4, G3 3 against 5; the modal-bell G3 page reads 7 of 14, graded once as first processed). E4 regains its ninth harmonic (-18.6 dB against the fundamental, against -54.3) and a smooth fall of H2 to H12, G3 holds 28 c sharp, and all three are closer to the recording only in the held part, because their 14 kPa attack is far brighter than the recording's

The attack is a stand-in. G3, Bb3 and E4 use the shape of one print at the card's own pressure level; F4, Bb4 and D5 start with a tongued attack of 14 kPa held for 0.8 s and relaxed over 0.5 s to their sustain (a gesture and not a measured value, and above the 4 to 13 kPa the card cites for high notes (Bouhuys, as quoted by Fletcher and Tarnopolsky 1999)); the sustains are the printed rule, 3.5 x 7 Pa/Hz x f (Fletcher and Tarnopolsky 1999: threshold p0 = K f with K = 7 Pa/Hz, loud playing at 3.3 to 3.9 times threshold): 8.56, 11.42 and 14.39 kPa on F4, Bb4 and D5, the D5 value above the cited range too. The print-shaped attack removed the 14 kPa overshoot, which was the brightest part of the old modal-bell clips (its centroid at 0.5 to 1.0 s was 15 to 21 % over the hold), so G3, Bb3 and E4 sit 0.1 to 0.6 dB farther from the recording in spectral distance (ties at 5, 5 and 4 of 14); the holds are unchanged and as dark as before

Brightness on the modal-bell pages: the hold centroids of the posted clips are 773 Hz (E4), 973 Hz (G3) and 992 Hz (Bb3), each with the q 1.4 row and the breath bore (the first clips read 613, 774 and 987 Hz, and Bb3 787 Hz without the q row), against the recordings' 1399, 1371 and 1398 Hz (the power-weighted mean frequency from 100 Hz to 6.9 kHz over 1.4 to 2.0 s of each clip; the simulated ones are the posted clips of deploys 542 (G3) and 568 (Bb3 and E4), read with the reader the pages use, the first clips those of deploys 390 and 410, the recordings the pages' own recording clips, with Bb3 checked against the raw Iowa note, 1398 Hz both ways), and E4's ninth harmonic nearly vanished on its first clip and was not re-read on the later ones

The shape of the flow noise: the row has no frequency shape of its own. On Bb3, with the q 1.4 row and before the breath bore, the floor between the harmonics re the strongest harmonic is 2 and 8 dB under the recording at 0.5 to 1 and 1 to 2 kHz and 3 and 20 dB over it at 2 to 4 and 4 to 6.9 kHz (the middle 0.7 s of the held note, the median power in the bins away from the harmonics; the recording is the raw Iowa note Trumpet.novib.mf.E3B3.aiff, 53.35 to 56.60 s). The law is an extrapolation from a large duct to a mouthpiece, and no level was set against any recording

A trumpeter's lip: the lip is an artificial latex lip measured on a trombone-size mouthpiece, its outward-striking mode only, with channel width and rest gap that are not a trumpeter's. No trumpet-player lip set is published. The G3, Bb3, E4 and D5 cards carry a lip_area_exponent line of 1.4 (borrowed from a trombonist; G3's 1.650 did not stay, see the summary); on Bb4 and F4 the aperture area is width times gap, because a q 1.4 render of each did not post (see the next entry), and F4 with the measured 1.900 did not sound its note. The trumpeter's lip data in print (searched 2026-11-09): Hruska, Svejda and Gustar (2015) give one semi-professional's lip opening in pixels with no conversion to mm2, and Yoshikawa (1995) was not open

The q = 1.4 row on the other two nonlinear pages did not post. Bb4 fell from 7 to 6 of 14 on a clip with no clipped sample (the first render at a full scale of 20 Pa clipped 319 samples and also read 6 of 14, so it was rendered again at 40 Pa; the hold is the same, +4.73 cents against the page): the fundamental frequency (14.0 to 19.1 cents) and the partial frequencies (0.68 to 2.22 cents) leave their rulers and the spectral centroid (8.76 to 3.01 semitones) enters. F4 was refused by the grader: the strongest line over 0.15 to 1.5 s is 457 Hz and the note is named from about 1.7 s (build-up 10, 50 and 90 % at 0.46, 0.59 and 2.03 s against 0.56, 0.74 and 0.81 s), the hold being +16.28 cents against the page

The recorded instrument: the Iowa trumpet is a Bach 180S37, whose printed main tube (.459 in = 11.66 mm) and bell (4 13/16 in = 122.24 mm) are on Bb3, E4, F4 and D5 (G3's and Bb4's live pages are earlier renders with the rounded profile diameters), but no numeric profile of it between those two diameters was found, so the 34 stations are a stand-in. That the stations were measured from a real commercial trumpet is now read from the paper (33 cones, maker and model not named). The mouthpiece is the station table's cup and throat, not a named one: a dealer's table prints a 16.20 mm cup for the Bach 7C shipped with the 180S37 against the table's 16.80 mm, but which mouthpiece the Iowa player used is not documented, so the cup is not replaced; searched 2026-11-09 for a printed profile: a shop-hosted copy of 'How to Select a Bach Trumpet' prints bore sizes and bell-flare sketches without dimensions; the Edinburgh MIMEd catalogue holds no Bach Stradivarius and its trumpet records are sparse points of other instruments (record 16621, a Boosey 'Bach Trumpet in A' of 1909: sounding length 1421 mm, minimum bore 9.8 mm, 11.7 mm at 711 mm, 16.5 mm at about 234 mm and 70 mm at 17.5 mm from the bell end; record 18495, a Glen cavalry trumpet of about 1850; record 49959, a valve trumpet of about 1840); Buick et al. (2002) measured laboratory leadpipe families; no side-on photograph with the printed 122.24 mm rim as the scale was found; Iowa's page names the instrument, the player (Aren Van Houzen), the date (16 May 2003) and the microphone (a Neumann KM 84 at 5 feet) but not the mouthpiece

Intonation: the stand-in bore's own resonances are not on the equal-tempered series, so each note's pre-stress is chosen from the emergent pitch of a first render. How a real Bach 180S37 would sit is unknown

Radiation and room: the receiver is a flanged half-space point 1.524 m on axis. The directivity of a real unflanged bell, the player's bell orientation and any room are not modelled. The modal-bell pages Bb3 and E4 run at 48 kHz in the engine and G3's page (an earlier render since 2026-11-10) at 32 kHz, resampled to 48 kHz for the grader (the V2 pages F4, Bb4 and D5 at 32 kHz), and the comparison is valid only below 6.9 kHz: the added rate is time resolution, not graded band

The bore gas on G3, Bb3 and E4 is one uniform steady full-breath state (27 C, saturated, 4.5 % CO2 and 16.5 % O2 of the dry gas, borrowed from the clarinet and oboe cards' woodwind sources), the same at the mouthpiece and the bell, with no profile along the bore, no wall heat transfer and no condensation, and the propagation is linear; the bore of F4, Bb4 and D5 holds dry air at 293.15 K, with no breath-warmed or humidified gas. Wall vibration is modelled on D5 only, by one uniform throat-clamped brass shell (its entry is among the present physics; what it lacks is the last entry below); on the other five pages, and for mutes, vibrato and the player's tonguing beyond the pressure gestures, it is not modelled. The finite mouth on D5 has no neck inertia, no lung and no tongue, its volume is another group's resting measurement and its opening another player's glottis, so the real upstream tract of the recorded player is in no page

The nonlinear bore's two-sided isentropic junction face at every radius step (8949d7341, in place of a one-sided step that lost about 1 % of the acoustic energy per traversal) was rendered on E4 and G3 and is not posted: E4 fell from 6 to 5 of 14 measures inside the ruler and G3 from 7 to 4 (3 strict against 7), and on G3 the hold pitch moved by -0.07 cent against the same card without the junction, inside the noise of the hold

A player's tract upstream of the lip (opt-in, landed in fs-couple brass_loop as a Thevenin source in series with the aperture, with the yielding wall and the constriction noise): with the digitized LOW tract of one trumpeter (Kaburagi, Yamada, Fukui and Minamiya 2011, Fig. 3, Eb4; a mouth pressure through a 20 ms one-pole, an ideal pressure source behind the glottis) no tract page posts. With rigid walls G3 and Bb3 do not start (the lip gap stays at 0.4955 and 0.4620 mm, 47 dB under the live clips) and E4 plays 360.9 Hz, 156 cents above E4, with its second harmonic strongest; removing the lip-end slice (section 0, the lip opening the vibrating aperture already represents) moves E4 by 0.6 Hz and changes nothing else. With the yielding wall of the voice cards (15.4 kg/m2, 3.79e5 Pa/m, 6.22e3 Pa s/m) G3 and E4 do not start (the E4 lip stays at its static opening of 0.404 mm) and Bb3 plays its note (234.33 Hz, 0.86 cent from the live clip, 1.03 dB louder) with an attack 2.8 times longer (10 to 90 percent in 285.6 ms against 102.25 ms): 3 of 14 measures inside against the live page's 5 of 14, the attack and the spectral flux leaving their rulers, so that page does not post. With the wall and the tract cut at section 0 Bb3 plays its note (234.50 Hz, 2.08 cents from the live clip, 0.11 dB louder) with an attack 3.7 times longer (10 to 90 percent in 379.94 ms against 102.25 ms) that starts 1.01 s later (the clip reaching 10 percent of its level at 1.29 s against the live clip's 0.28 s), and with 4.7, 10.8 and 5.1 dB less energy at 6 to 8, 8 to 12 and 12 to 16 kHz in the held note: 5 of 14 measures inside against the live page's 5 of 14, the attack leaving its ruler and the harmonics-to-noise ratio entering it; that entry comes from the grader's sustain window taking in the slow onset (38.70 to 34.78 dB while an approximate comb reading of the steady stretch rises 2.6 dB on the same two clips), so that page posts as a tie with its onset named in its lead. In a Zwikker-Kosten chain model that matches the render's DC resistance and admission margin to 0.2 percent, the rigid tract's input impedance is 3.8e6 and 5.4e6 Pa s/m3, mostly reactive (real parts 2.2e5 and 3.4e5), at 196 and 233 Hz, and it carries a peak of 1.16e8 Pa s/m3 at 349 Hz, 19 Hz above E4; that peak belongs to the rendered construction (rigid walls, an ideal source behind the glottis neck); with the wall the peak is 4.65e7 at 416 Hz and the values at 196, 233 and 330 Hz are 2.7e6, 3.5e6 and 7.9e6 Pa s/m3. Fig. 4 of Kaburagi et al. 2011 (raster, read by eye) shows, for the same area function with wall losses, a subglottal tube and a lung terminal, a first peak of about 1e7 Pa s/m3 near 330 Hz and about 4e6 to 5e6 Pa s/m3 at 196 to 233 Hz; a Weibel subglottal tube built from the printed morphology puts its own resonances 219 to 249 Hz under Ishizaka's measured 640, 1400 and 2100 Hz, so the paper's tube is not reproducible from printed data, and the wall differs from the paper's (the paper holds its wall constant, equal to this wall on a 4.03 cm2 section, while the row scales it with perimeter over area, so it acts more strongly on the narrow sections; the row's damping over mass is within 1.1 percent of the paper's, and its stiffness over mass is 2.77 times the paper's, a wall resonance of 25.0 against 15.0 Hz, both far below the notes). The paper's own blowing simulation (Adachi-Sato lips, blowing pressures set per lip frequency to obtain stable vibration, 3.0 kPa at 220 to 260 Hz) found only a very slight change of vibration frequency with this tract and a lower starting pressure for every mode except the second (234 Hz); the G3, Bb3 and E4 pages then live grow at 7, 19 and 13 per second (G3's live page has since been replaced by its earlier render, whose growth rate was not re-read) (sigma over omega 0.0056, 0.013 and 0.0062), and no single tract quantity at the note (real part, reactance or magnitude) separates the pages that start from the pages that do not

What D5's brass-shell bell wall does not carry: the 500 to 800 Hz band, in which Gorman, Rokni, Moore, Kausel and Chatziioannou (ISMA 2014, Le Mans, pp. 215 to 218; a straight bell of the Spiri Corporation, not a trumpet) measured two broad mechanical resonances and posited that "these axial resonances are broad-band and are responsible for the audible effects" (the sentence's first words are left out of the quotation, which is otherwise exact), because the shell has no axisymmetric mode below 1031 Hz; a mount other than the one assumed clamp at the throat; a non-uniform wall, a rim bead, braces and the player's hand; radiation of the shell into the outside air; and the loss that would broaden the modes. The wall is on D5 only; G3, Bb3, E4, F4 and Bb4 do not carry it.
